I’ll run the scan and check the source to distinguish merge blockers from maintenance warnings and false positives.

The scan found the same 39 findings, but local history changed their ordering and risk scores. I’ll use the IDs and scores in your supplied report for the review. Source inspection also caught an incorrect warning: `describeCheckout` already has a named, explicit options type.

**Block merge: 6 findings; warn: 25; ignore: 8.**

I ran `crimes scan --format json`: it returned 39 findings (5 high, 17 medium, 17 low). Local history changed ordering and some scores, so **the IDs and `agent_risk` values below follow your supplied report**, matched to the source by fingerprint.

I’m treating this as an application PR under your scenario. All findings are newly introduced against the empty baseline. Severity and agent risk inform priority; confirmed behavior determines whether something blocks merge.

| ID (`crime_…`) | Finding | Severity / agent risk | Category | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00001 | Direct clock reads — `date.ts` | medium / 0.45 | **warn** | Highest reported agent risk: expiry and calendar behavior depend on wall time. Inject a clock for deterministic boundary tests; direct clock access alone does not prove incorrect behavior. |
| 00002 | Return shape roulette | low / 0.44 | **warn** | Relatively high agent risk despite low severity: success, error, and redirect results lack a consistent discriminator. Name and discriminate the variants. |
| 00003 | Missing agent context | medium / 0.43 | **warn** | Meaningful maintenance risk warrants documenting commands and conventions. Missing agent-specific instructions is not an application correctness failure. |
| 00004 | Scattered `"enterprise"` literal | medium / 0.43 | **warn** | Cross-file edits can drift, but repeated labels do not establish duplicated policy. Share the domain definition where semantics genuinely match. |
| 00005 | Mixed UTC/local methods | high / 0.39 | **block merge** | `dateLabel()` combines a UTC year with local month/day, producing inconsistent dates near year boundaries. High severity is supported by an actual correctness defect. |
| 00006 | Duplicate navigation sources | medium / 0.39 | **warn** | “Plans” and “Billing” can drift during edits. Establish canonical metadata or document deliberate contextual labels; navigation still targets the same route. |
| 00007 | Route metadata drift | medium / 0.39 | **warn** | Competing page names increase maintenance risk. Align user-facing terminology; differing component and route names alone are not failures. |
| 00008 | Broad options bag | low / 0.39 | **ignore** | The source already declares `CheckoutOptions` with all six required fields. The claimed implicit shape is false; the score does not justify splitting a coherent typed parameter. |
| 00009 | Direct clock reads — `billing.ts` | medium / 0.38 | **warn** | Inject a clock around discount thresholds. The scanner understates impact: `daysSince` feeds pricing and upgrade branches indirectly, contrary to its “record or render” claim. |
| 00010 | Timezone-unsafe parsing | medium / 0.38 | **warn** | The timezone-free datetime needs an explicit intended zone. However, the date-only ISO literal parses as UTC; the report overgeneralizes. Clarify semantics before changing either. |
| 00011 | `User` contract drift | high / 0.37 | **warn** | High severity warrants checking the relationship, but missing fields in a smaller record do not prove incompatibility. Use an explicit projection if these represent the same entity. |
| 00012 | `Invoice` contract drift | high / 0.37 | **warn** | Money and identifier omissions deserve scrutiny, but the shared fields agree. A summary record can legitimately omit details; establish the contract before requiring unification. |
| 00013 | Negative flags | low / 0.37 | **ignore** | Two plainly readable negations do not establish a defect. The maintenance score alone does not justify renaming the public parameters. |
| 00014 | Side effects in refund preview | medium / 0.35 | **block merge** | A preview unconditionally invokes audit and email operations. The moderate scores understate the concrete risk of callers triggering effects when requesting a calculation. Separate preview calculation from execution. |
| 00015 | Refund rule only in a comment | medium / 0.35 | **warn** | No nearby owner/support guard implements the stated policy. Establish where enforcement belongs; this function does not itself demonstrate an executed unauthorized refund. |
| 00016 | Millisecond day arithmetic | medium / 0.33 | **warn** | `tomorrowMs()` adds exactly 24 hours. That is valid elapsed-time arithmetic but can violate “same local time tomorrow.” Define the contract and test DST boundaries if calendar semantics are intended. |
| 00017 | Hardcoded localhost | medium / 0.31 | **block merge** | `adminUrl()` always returns a development address. This concrete portability failure warrants blocking despite moderate scores; supply the deployment URL through configuration. |
| 00018 | Hardcoded home path | medium / 0.31 | **block merge** | Schema loading depends on one developer’s checkout and otherwise returns `null`. Resolve a packaged resource or configured path before merge. |
| 00019 | Tenant terminology aliases | medium / 0.31 | **warn** | Vocabulary can mislead future edits, but organisation, account, and team may represent distinct levels. Document their relationships before consolidating names. |
| 00020 | Direct clock read — `state.ts` | low / 0.29 | **ignore** | The expression is the isolated example `Date.now() > 0`; no actual expiration policy is evidenced. Introducing clock infrastructure here is unjustified. |
| 00021 | Date string concatenation | low / 0.29 | **block merge** | Source confirms `getMonth()` is printed without adding one, so January renders as month zero. This proven output bug outweighs the low scores; fix alongside 00005. |
| 00022 | Default locale | low / 0.29 | **ignore** | A display helper may intentionally use the runtime locale. No fixed-locale or serialization contract establishes that this behavior is wrong. |
| 00023 | Singular/plural mismatch | low / 0.29 | **warn** | `users` is scalar and `invoice` is an array. Rename to communicate the existing shapes; do not change types merely to satisfy names. |
| 00024 | Orphan `/account/subscription` | low / 0.29 | **warn** | Verify the intended entry point. Missing static references does not prove a route is unreachable through direct links or framework routing. |
| 00025 | Orphan `/team` | low / 0.29 | **warn** | Check discoverability and intended navigation; low severity and incomplete reachability evidence do not justify blocking or deletion. |
| 00026 | Orphan `/workspace/members` | low / 0.29 | **warn** | Confirm the members journey has an entry point. Static-reference absence is insufficient evidence of a broken route. |
| 00027 | Test without assertions | medium / 0.28 | **warn** | The test calls an empty local helper and protects no behavior. Replace it with an observable assertion; it cannot support confidence in billing correctness. |
| 00028 | Commented-out implementation | medium / 0.27 | **warn** | Disabled refund code invites accidental reuse. Remove or explain it, but inactive text does not itself cause a runtime defect. |
| 00029 | Broken documentation link | low / 0.25 | **warn** | The missing setup guide demonstrably interrupts onboarding. Repair the link; its limited impact does not warrant blocking the application. |
| 00030 | Weak invoice assertion | low / 0.24 | **warn** | The test checks truthiness of a locally fabricated object rather than production invoice behavior. Improve coverage without treating this as proof of a billing failure. |
| 00031 | Undeclared `vitest` | low / 0.24 | **block merge** | The test imports a package absent from the manifest. A clean standalone install cannot supply the test dependency; declare it as a development dependency and make testing reproducible. |
| 00032 | Swallowed error | low / 0.16 | **ignore** | In the current implementation, the body is always nonempty and there is no mail-service call. The reported lost email failure is hypothetical; revisit when real sending is implemented. |
| 00033 | 204-line function | high / 0.13 | **warn** | High structural severity merits extracting cohesive pricing and presentation helpers. Low agent risk and length alone do not establish a release-blocking defect. |
| 00034 | Dense TODOs — `todo.ts` | medium / 0.10 | **warn** | Review unfinished storage and eviction semantics, especially periodic clearing. Marker density itself is a weak release criterion; deleting comments would not resolve the underlying questions. |
| 00035 | Embedded raster in SVG | high / 0.08 | **warn** | Check fidelity at intended display sizes. Despite high scanner severity, the asset is only 592 bytes and SVG legitimately supports embedded images; no substantial performance failure is demonstrated. |
| 00036 | 310-line file | medium / 0.07 | **ignore** | Barely exceeding a 300-line threshold supplies little additional evidence. Responsibility problems are already covered by 00033; avoid arbitrary file splitting. |
| 00037 | 254 KB hero image | low / 0.05 | **warn** | Consider compression against rendered dimensions and the page budget. Low severity and agent risk support optimization follow-up, not blocking without measured impact. |
| 00038 | 32×32 raster icon | low / 0.05 | **ignore** | Dimensions alone do not prove poor fidelity or excessive size. PNG can be appropriate; require an actual rendering or asset-budget problem before replacement. |
| 00039 | TODO density — `billing.ts` | low / 0.04 | **ignore** | Four markers barely exceed the threshold. Assess their underlying behavior separately; the count adds negligible review risk. |

The six blocking findings include two reports about the same date formatter, which should be resolved together.

The supplied coverage report also notes an excluded suppression file and a superseded suppression fingerprint. Neither means the underlying issue is fixed. Review the pin migration separately; disabled detectors and excluded files limit what this scan establishes.
